findings.scope: Compact offline trace findings for baseline and isolated velocity-input slew comparison. No new simulator run, build, or source edit. All statistics are observed from one fresh-world trial per profile, not repeatability proof.

summary.S0: New binary defaults disabled all optional tuning; right03 completed20s without motor warning, but raw target contact acceleration spikes persist and can exceed the older failed baseline. Do not attribute its one-run pass causally to history seeding.
summary.S1: Only velocity-reference slew400rad/s^2 changes. Per-update WBC/motor dq increment bound is observed throughout valid motion; q targets remain unchanged; hip feedforward peaks fall. This is velocity input shaping and does not enforce derivative consistency of the nominal q trajectory.
summary.window_assumption: A=100rad/s^2 and24ms are engineering assumptions. Actual sampled delta-q/delta-dq trajectories frequently leave those reachable sets. Conservative L1 PD bounds cover more than those state sets, but still miss some sampled packets and cannot provide a continuous torque guarantee.

definitions.qdd_stat: Finite difference of successive exported WBC joint velocity targets over actual trace step, normally2ms; not measured physical acceleration. all_active includes valid MPC_STANCE/TROT. trot_contact excludes stance transitions.
definitions.position_velocity_difference: Average endpoint raw/limited dq minus interval finite difference of unchanged nominal q target. Raw MPC dq includes state feedback; nominal q can move on a new policy. This discrepancy metric does not itself prove an implementation defect.
definitions.feedforward: QP feedforward before host/actuator scaling; excludes motor PD and friction.
definitions.window: For each eligible valid Trot sender, compare max sampled q/dq change over next24ms with |dq_now|H+0.5AH^2 and AH. Compare reconstructed fixed-packet PD/total effort over0-24ms and conservative20-24ms delivery/hold probe. Feedback trace is500Hz; actual force peaks are logged at1kHz.
definitions.complete_window_exclusion: Exclude incomplete24ms windows, trace gaps>3ms and any future interval interrupted by FAULT. The causal failure packet in B0 is among excluded windows; its authoritative1kHz warning remains a failure regardless of the complete-window coverage statistics.

reconstructed_packet_validation.semantics: Command reconstructed from the nearest pre-creation control trace plus sampled actuator L1 scaling; evaluated at authoritative1kHz warning physical q,dq, not an interpolated state.

limitations: Single-run S0/S1 results cannot establish robustness or a safe real-hardware envelope.
Sampled500Hz feedback misses between-sample acceleration/effort peaks. Reconstructed hypothetical packet torques are evaluated on recorded trajectories; commands are not re-simulated.
A100 instantaneous violations do not imply every full24ms integrated bound fails, so both are reported separately.
The20-24ms execution probe is a conservative modeling window around observed22ms control-to-application timing, not measured physical motor latency.
The public controller defaults and future candidate selection are decided separately by root; this artifact reports measurements only.

semantics.units: joint-side SI; nominal limits [23.7,23.7,45] Nm repeat each leg
semantics.sampling: 500 Hz control trace, not continuous physical motor torque or measured actuator gains
semantics.H0: S1 pre-QP reserve is zero and host scale is initialized to one because the new guard is bypassed; that is not proof the existing hardware sampled L1 guard never scales.
semantics.actuator_reconstruction: Use exported Trot q/dq/Kp/Kd, WBC FF times host scale and same-frame feedback; reconstruct existing hardware sampled L1 scaling algebraically. Trot has no stand-up blend. This is not actual packet telemetry, ignores float quantization and does not infer 1 kHz inter-sample saturation.
semantics.FF_cap: S3 cap is nominal limit minus reported PD reservation. S1 cap is nominal limit. Near-cap counts alone do not establish causality of pose or tracking differences.
semantics.window_assumption: H=.024 s,A=100 rad/s2,f=.35 is an engineering profile, not identification or proof of real acceleration/latency bounds.

interpretation: On the completed S3 right03 trial, the pre-QP governor scales at least one joint in most motion frames, whereas final host guard scaling is absent. PD gain reduction is therefore a persistent behavior change, not merely rare peak clipping.
The FF hard upper bounds rarely bind directly on either recorded trajectory; it is not supported to attribute the observed lower height solely to FF saturation.

S1 has only a few reconstructed existing actuator sampled rescaling events. S3 removes those events on this run but introduces substantial gain adaptation, and tracking/height results do not justify enabling this window profile as a default.
One trial per profile, different closed-loop trajectories and unverified A assumptions prevent a causal or hardware conclusion.

A failed/unfinished motion receives no invented steady state. Low height after FAULT is separated from active-support height behavior.
Motor warnings are simulated requested torque, not measured motor torque or contact force; no continuous saturation model or real-current calibration was added.
The1.10-times protection threshold differs from nominal URDF effort limits. No WARN does not prove all requests are below nominal limits.
Engineering delay/acceleration assumptions, planned contacts and estimator trust are not measured hardware delay or measured foot contact.
QP joint-acceleration objective changes base-only tracking into momentum-rate tracking. Corrected effective-height acceleration residuals do not by themselves prove realized body height.
Velocity input slew preserves q references and shares limited dq with WBC/motor, but does not enforce q_des derivative equals dq_des.

Bounded cross-track memory limits estimated position-reference debt; it is not a bound on true-world displacement. Original failed tracking trials remain failed even when alternate-frame analysis explains geometry.
Task-file R velocity weights are transformed by the initial foot Jacobian at runtime; the listed complete diagonals are file values, not a claim that runtime R is diagonal.
Build and communication success do not constitute real robot motion acceptance. No stand/walk commands were sent to hardware.
